1

Details

Prompted by Pierfrancesco's comment on the budget page (2026-10-16): "if we buy the plastic plate and we produce the detector, the cost for each can be within 2 [k]euros each, 8 [k]euros for all the 4" (Scionix), PMTs borrowed again.

Deciding: built how, how thick, one piece or two

The plate sits where the 20 × 30 cm bars were; it closes the trigger leg and measures E_sum

Hover the dotted terms and the points on each chart for values and sources.

2

Details

Each arm: Micromegas TPC → SiPM wall (all 20 bars read) → one big plate, read at both ends along the beam through fishtail guides. The plate replaces the two 20 × 30 × 2 cm bars, which accepted 2.3 % of X17 pairs; 78 × 80 cm plates accept ~14 % (TRIGGER_OPTIONS §2).

The questions here: buy finished or build in-house; 2, 4 or 5 cm; one plate or two bars per arm; and whether the thicker plate fires too often on γ.

3

Details

Model: costs.py (piece_cost_diy, arms_diy). Raw plate 0.064–0.3 €/cm³ (central 0.13).

  • Low end: Pierfrancesco/Scionix, ~€2k per plate. That is consistent with cast scintillator at ~$40/kg in 2001 (NIM A 466, 482), ≈ €65/kg today.
  • High end: CERN 2025, an 80 × 80 × 2 cm EJ-200 sheet at 6k CHF (indico 1546121).
  • Scionix has built 5 cm, 0.5–1 m² EJ-200 panels (Felsenkeller veto, arXiv:2301.03905).

Per piece, central: edge finishing €300, wrapping €150/m², cement €100, guide €600–1000 each (Eljen/Shalom make them to order), housing €800. Extra PMTs (economy 2"): €600, from Pierfrancesco's LS rebuild (16 PMTs + cases €7k). Workshop labour is in kind and not counted.

Ask Pierfrancesco: is the €2k for 78 × 80 × 5 cm, and PVT or polystyrene? Which tubes are the borrowed 8 (2" or 3")?

4

Details

optics_toy.py --refresh → out/optics_refresh.csv. A photon ray-trace: TIR (0.98 per bounce, 0.95 for edges polished in-house), Al-foil wrap, fishtail guides with étendue loss, PMT QE and TTS. Bulk attenuation: 2.5 m for PVT, 1 m for polystyrene (UPS-923A/ZEPLIN-III). Absolute pe/MeV are optimistic by ~1.5–2×: treat them as a ranking.

Light per MeV falls because the same PMT covers a smaller fraction of a thicker end face. The lepton deposit grows with thickness, so pe per lepton falls more slowly than 1/T. Width is not the issue either: 78 cm with both ends read is 4–5 % (PVT). Light is lost along the 80 cm length.

Polystyrene's non-uniformity is a smooth function of hit position, which the Micromegas measure. It can be mapped with cosmics, but it eats into the energy resolution.

Splitting a plate in two doubles the light per bar and halves the rate per channel

5

Details

Same PMT on half the end face → ×2 light per MeV, and shorter guides → less time spread. Uniformity stays set by the material.

Seams (sim/accept/seams.csv, Geant4 T1 entry points): with N = 2, 3.9 % of accepted legs land within 1 cm of the seam, 9.7 % within 2.5 cm. E_sum sums both bars, so only a per-bar trigger threshold would care. The wrap gap is ~2 mm, 0.5 % of the area.

Cost: +8 PMTs, +4 guides, +4 housings ≈ +€11k. The polystyrene single plate on the borrowed 2" tubes is the weakest point (~240 ps in the toy, worse in reality); a split, 3" tubes or PVT each bring it under 200 ps.

6

Details

Why the threshold cannot scale with thickness: the X17 leptons stop in the plate. An accepted lepton leaves a median 7.6 MeV even in 10 cm (middle half 4.7–10.8), so 4 MeV would cost 35 % and 3 MeV 15 %.

γ toy (gamma_toy.py, an analytic stand-in): Klein–Nishina Compton, pair production, straight-line electrons, no energy smearing. Use 2.7–3 MeV where ²⁰⁸Tl dominates. Normalised per µSv/h with ICRP 74 h*(10). The total per arm does not change with a split; per channel it falls as 1/N.

Hard γ (Fe/Al/¹⁴N capture, ³He(n,γ), ⁸Be) pass any usable threshold. For them only shielding, a split, or a thinner plate help.

7

Details

Runs finished 2026-10-02 but were analysed only now (sim/bkg/*.json, bkg_figs.py). G is the window in which a foreign slab deposit piles onto a pair's E_sum. It is ~10 ns with waveform digitizers on the plate PMTs and 50–100 ns with a shaping QDC. Splitting the plate into N bars divides the effective G by N.

Slab singles per arm above 1.67 MeV: 0.23 MHz as built, 0.33 MHz with P5L/P5B, mostly air ¹⁴N(n,γ). The 2 cm plate (P2) is worse than as built: more area for cosmics and accidentals without the calorimetry.

Missing: the bare 5 cm plate (P5). Its C1w contract was never produced. Unwrapped, it makes ~2×10⁷ H(n,γ)/s at 10¹⁰ absorbed n/s. A 2.5 MeV threshold would hide those from the leg, but not from pile-up.

Ask first

Pierfrancesco: is the €2k for 78 × 80 × 5 cm, PVT or polystyrene? Which tubes are the 8 borrowed ones? Scionix quote in writing.

Then build

One prototype plate on the cosmic bench, with the Micromegas giving position: anchors the light toy, and measures the hall γ rate above 2.5 MeV.

Not covered here

The neutron sensitivity of the plastic (n–p recoils) at fast-neutron sites; a two-bar Geant4 geometry; hall γ at any site (no facility has given a dose rate).
